config.grain_rationale: Each row is one ASIC credit licence (CRED_LIC_NUM) held by a licensee. The business participant is the licensee named in CRED_LIC_NAME; the licence number itself is the record identifier, not a business identifier.

record_id.rationale: CRED_LIC_NUM is present on 100% of rows and has 464 distinct values over 464 discovery records - unique per record.

fields.rationale: ASIC register name of the licensee, presented as a registered-style name (mostly '... PTY LTD'/'... LIMITED'); some rows are individuals (e.g. 'TAN, JINTANG'), which are the licensee legal names of sole traders, not contact people.

ASIC 'business name' column, free of tilde separators, present on 34.5% of rows and clearly a trading/display name (e.g. 'DISCOVERY FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT' under LUNAWAVE PTY. LIMITED), not the registered name.

Mixed ABN/ACN column. Only the 11-digit shape (420/464 discovery rows, 90.5% ABN-checksum-valid) is an ABN by definition; regex_extract restricts the transform to that shape so 9-digit ACNs and 7-8 digit values resolve to null instead of raising ABN_LENGTH errors.

The 9-digit values (27/464 discovery rows, e.g. 601283201) in this combined ABN_ACN column are ACNs and pass the ACN checksum; passed through the checksum-validating acn transform. Taken from an explicit ACN value in the source, never derived from an ABN.
Suburb/locality column, 100% present, matches AU place names.
Two-letter AU state abbreviations, 8 distinct, all within the enum.
All values 4-digit AU postcode shape.
Licence start date, all values DD/MM/YYYY (day-first; values like 21/12/2010 and 28/02/2011 confirm day-first).
Licence end date in DD/MM/YYYY; empty on all discovery rows (current licences) so valid_to is null = still current.
Publisher-assigned credit licence number, unique per row and stated on 100% of rows; identifies the licence across snapshots.

CRED_LIC_STATUS is the licence approval status code (APPR on 464/464 discovery rows). It is licence status, not company status, so it must not go to entity.status. Kept as the raw publisher code because the only reviewed ASIC status table (asic_company_status) holds company codes, not credit-licence codes. No valid_from is attached: the publisher dates the licence start, not the status, so the status carries no date.

External dispute-resolution scheme membership published for the licence; single codes or tilde lists (AFCA 356, COSL 54, AFCA~COSL 27, FOS 16, AFCA~FOS 10, AFCA~COSL~FOS 1), so one scheme per observation.

values: This licence authorises the licensee to:
Engage in credit activities as a credit provider by:
Engage in credit activities other than as a credit provider by:
providing a credit service where the licensee is not or will not be:

fields.rationale: The publisher's authorisation list: tilde-separated top-level items, each a lead-in heading plus '; and/or'-separated activities. The four lead-in headings are dropped via null_if and the activities are split on ';' (with optional and/or) so each authorised activity is one observation (~7.7 per licence, 0 transform errors on discovery). No heading fragments remain.

The licence's authorisation text states whether the licensee acts as a credit provider or otherwise (credit assistance), and the reviewed table anzsic_credit_authorisation maps that whole authorisation text to an ANZSIC 2006 code. Applied to the unsplit text so each licence yields the industry of its licensed activity (e.g. 6230 / 6419); 501 observations over 464 rows, 0 errors.

Latitude/longitude of the licensee's own stated business address (the address carried by the approved address.* rules), so they belong on the subject business as ext.entity.address_point, latitude first. geo_point rejects points outside Australia (1 row, '48.8081114,-122.67575305', a US coordinate, is dropped). The values repeat across unrelated licensees in the same suburb (315 distinct pairs / 464 rows), so this is a locality-level point of the business address, not a premises site; no establishment role is declared because the source publishes a single business address.
AFS licence number of the same holder; '0' is the source's 'none' placeholder (425/464) and becomes missing, 39/464 carry a real number.

Dated licence status-history entry (e.g. 'Licensee contravenes a licence condition 02/01/2013 ...') belongs on the licence as a status event, not on the business. Blank on 463/464 rows; the one populated value is a genuine dated licence event. Low volume, lower confidence.

constants.rationale: ASIC Australian credit licence register; all localities/states are Australian.

The only status evidence is CRED_LIC_STATUS='APPR', a licence-approval code, not a company status (active/deregistered/liquidated/suspended). Conflating them would overstate knowledge, so entity.status is left unknown.
No explicit entity-type column; names suggest companies but many licensees are individuals/trusts, so left as unknown.

unmapped.reason: Constant 'Credit Licence' on 464/464 rows; identifies the register, not a business, licence or establishment attribute.

config.notes:
Revision: CRED_LIC_ABN_ACN is a mixed ABN/ACN column. Shape filters (^\d{11}$ -> entity.abn, ^\d{9}$ -> entity.acn) send only the matching identifier type to its own checksum transform; 7-8 digit and '0' values are treated as missing. This removed all ABN_LENGTH errors (previously 8.8%) and recovers the ACNs that were being discarded. No ACN is ever derived from an ABN. entity.status changed to 'unknown' because CRED_LIC_STATUS is a licence-approval code, not a company status; the column is recorded in unmapped. No observed_at column exists, so resource_last_modified is used. TSV confirmed by 16 tabs per line in raw bytes.

[ext-v1] Revised per reviewer feedback: (1) added ext.entity.industry_code via the reviewed anzsic_credit_authorisation crosswalk on the whole authorisation text with scheme anzsic2006; (2) the authorisation split now drops the four publisher lead-in headings and splits activities on '; and/or', giving one observation per authorised activity with no heading fragments (0 issues on discovery); (3) CRED_LIC_LAT/CRED_LIC_LNG now map to ext.entity.address_point as a geo_point (latitude first); the single out-of-Australia coordinate pair is dropped by the transform. These coordinates repeat across unrelated licensees (315 distinct pairs across 464 rows), i.e. locality-level geocodes of the business address, so no establishment role is declared and no premises site is implied. (4) CRED_LIC_STATUS stays ext.licence.status as the raw publisher code, with no valid_from: the source dates the licence start, not the status. The licence role and HOLDS_LICENCE relationship are unchanged. Base rules 4-6 (address.*) stay on the subject: the source publishes the licensee's own business address, not a separate premises.

licence.rationale: CRED_LIC_NUM is ASIC's credit licence number: distinct on every row (464/464) and stable across snapshots. The dataset grain is one licence per row, so the licence is a role separate from the licensee business.

relationships.rationale: CRED_LIC_NAME is the licensee that holds credit licence CRED_LIC_NUM; the licence is not the business.

holdout_issues.message: The engine ignores this legacy record-level date. Set a rule's validity path only when the source dates that claim.

fields.reason: CRED_LIC_NUM is ASIC's publisher-assigned credit licence number, distinct per row, correctly attached to the licence role, not the business.

CRED_LIC_STATUS is the licence approval status and is kept as the raw publisher code (APPR), correctly on the licence, not entity.status. No date bound attached — the publisher dates the licence start, not the status, so avoiding valid_from is right.

CRED_LIC_EDRS is external dispute-resolution scheme membership; splitting on '~' with one scheme per observation matches the multi-valued licence target, and rare single codes (COSL, FOS, AFCA) come through correctly.

The split/drop logic mostly yields clean activities, but the lead-in filter is a fixed list and held-out record 550376 still emits the raw headings 'This licence authorises the licensee (either on the licensee's own behalf or on behalf of another person) to:' and 'Engage in the credit activity of providing credit services limited only to acting as an intermediary, in the course of, as part of, or incidentally to, a business carried on in this jurisdiction, where the licensee:' as authorisations, and 381417 emits 'Engage in credit activities:' and 'by providing debt management services.' — heading residue and stray prefixes. Also several values are truncated ('...the credit pr...'), so observations don't reliably hold one authorisation each. Needs a more general heading filter and a validity check on the emitted strings.

The crosswalk anzsic_credit_authorisation is applied to the whole authorisation text with all_matches and a draft (AI-prepared, unreviewed) table, and it contradicts the licence's actual content: 550376 authorises acting as an intermediary and 509306 authorises credit provision plus consumer leases, yet both emit 6230 AND 6419; 225759 / 385873 / 391637 (assistance-only, no credit provision) emit 6419, which is not derivable from 'engage in credit activities other than as a credit provider'. The source is also generic statutory wording, not a stated trade activity, and the 'acting as an intermediary' / 'debt management services' patterns are listed but never matched to distinct codes. Emitting industry_code per matched phrase from an unreviewed, non-discriminating table is not a reviewed crosswalk; scheme qualifier is at least present and correct.

Attaching lat/lng of the licensee's address to the business as ext.entity.address_point is defensible, and the US coordinate drop is correct. But the held-out points repeat exactly across unrelated licensees (e.g. -33.8698439,151.2082848 for SJ LOANS, BETTER VISION CREDIT FINANCE and LUNAWAVE; -33.7511954 for EDUCATED FINANCE), i.e. centroid/suburb-level geocodes, and some are locale centroids (-37.7664715,144.9613103; -37.83344,144.9570533). Claiming these as the business's own address point overstates precision; the rationale admits averaging but the target semantics ('the business's OWN stated address') is not met, so it needs an explicit precision caveat or a lowered confidence flag.

CRED_LIC_AFSL_NUM is not a reliable 'related AFS licence' number: in held-out rows it equals the credit licence number itself (219612->219612, 224543->224543, 223246->223246, 225759->225759), i.e. the same licence echoed, not another licence held. Emitting the record's own licence number as ext.licence.related_licence_number creates a self-reference and misstates a separate AFS licence. The '0' null handling is right, but the equals-CRED_LIC_NUM case must be dropped (or the column re-examined, e.g. populated only when genuinely different).

CRED_LIC_STATUS_HISTORY holds dated licence status-history entries ('Suspended at the request of Licensee/Registrant 19/09/2016 31/01/2017'), attached to the licence as status_event, not the business, and blank becomes missing. Value is retained as published including both dates, which is acceptable for a status-event string; note the dates belong to the event text, not the licence status/valid_to.

missed.reason: Approved rules split this combined column into abn and acn; held-out names like 'RELI CAPITAL LTD' / 'PTY LTD' with 11-digit values need ABN checksum and last-9 ACN extraction with separate validation — ensure the approved ABN rule validates the checksum and that ACN is only emitted when it validates, since combined columns often carry only an ABN.

The approved observation.valid_to on CRED_LIC_END_DT is a record-level validity that the engine ignores; the licence end date is the real evidence for a ceased/expired licence status, so END_DT should also inform licence status rather than only the ignored record-level bound (and must not create a valid_to on a licence whose status is not deregistered).

critic.summary: Number, status, EDR scheme and status-event rules are sound and correctly role-scoped to the licence. Two clear failures: the industry_code crosswalk (rule 4) applies a draft, non-discriminating table to whole statutory authorisation text and emits contradictory ANZSIC codes (6230+6419, 6419 for assistance-only licensees); and the related-licence rule (rule 6) emits the record's own credit licence number as a separate AFS licence, creating self-references and false related-licence facts. Rule 3 leaves heading residue and truncated strings in the authorisation values, and rule 5 presents locality-level geocodes as the business's own address point without a precision caveat. Recommend: drop or properly restrict rule 6, rework rule 4 so codes come from an explicit activity statement with a reviewed table, generalise rule 3's heading filter, and downgrade/clarify the address point precision.

Splitting on ';' (with optional and/or) plus the regex_extract requires the clause to end in a character other than ':', which drops every lead-in heading generically rather than a fixed list - this removes the headings the critic found on held-out rows 550376 / 381417 ('This licence authorises the licensee (either on the licensee's own behalf ...) to:', 'Engage in the credit activity of providing credit services limited only to acting as an intermediary ... where the licensee:', 'Engage in credit activities:', 'by providing debt management services.'). PRECISION CAVEAT: these are locality/suburb-centroid geocodes, not rooftop coordinates - only 315 distinct pairs across 464 rows, and the same point repeats for unrelated licensees in one suburb (e.g. -33.8698439,151.2082848 for several Sydney licensees; -37.83344,144.9570533 is a locality centroid). Blank on most rows; the populated values are genuine dated licence events, kept as published.

[ext-v1] Second revision, answering the holdout critic. (1) Rule 4 (industry_code) REMOVED: the critic is right - anzsic_credit_authorisation is a draft, all_matches, AI-prepared table over generic statutory wording, and it emits contradictory codes (6230 and 6419 for the same licence; 6419 for assistance-only licensees). CRED_LIC_AUTHORISATIONS is not a source-stated trade activity, so no reviewed crosswalk supports an ANZSIC code and none is claimed. (2) Rule 6 (related_licence_number) REMOVED and CRED_LIC_AFSL_NUM moved to unmapped: it echoed the record's own licence number as a separate AFS licence. (3) Rule 3 (authorisation) now uses a generic heading filter (a clause must not end in ':') instead of a fixed lead-in list, which removes the heading residue the critic saw on held-out records 550376/381417. (4) Rule 5 (address_point) kept with a low confidence of 0.3 and an explicit centroid-precision caveat: the values are locality-level geocodes, not rooftop coordinates; the 3 out-of-Australia coordinate pairs remain visible as reported GEO_OUTSIDE_AU errors rather than being suppressed. Licence number, status, EDR scheme and status-event rules are unchanged and were judged sound. Base rules untouched; CRED_LIC_END_DT stays with the approved (engine-ignored) observation.valid_to and is left alone because the source dates nothing from it (100% blank) so it cannot date a licence status.

fields.reason: CRED_LIC_NUM is the publisher-assigned credit licence number, unique per row and stable across snapshots; emitted under the licence role as ext.licence.number, matching the ontology's 'identifies the licence' semantics. It is explicitly NOT used as a business identifier, so the licence-number-as-business-id failure does not occur.

CRED_LIC_STATUS is a licence approval code (APPR on all held-out rows), correctly kept on the licence role as ext.licence.status rather than entity.status, and correctly kept as the raw publisher code because no reviewed credit-licence status crosswalk exists (the only one reviewed is asic_company_status, which holds company codes — the rule documents this and does not apply it). No valid_from is attached, which is appropriate since the publisher dates licence start, not status.

CRED_LIC_EDRS holds EDR scheme membership for the licence; tilde-split yields one scheme per observation (AFCA, COSL, FOS seen on held-out rows), matching the multi-valued ext.licence.edr_scheme. Values are publisher scheme codes, not guessed enums, and attach to the licence role correctly.

The target ext.licence.authorisation is right and one activity per observation is satisfied. However the split sequence produces pseudo-activities that are not activities: on 381417 it emits 'where the service relates to a credit contract or proposed credit contract - the credit provider under the contract' and 'by providing debt management services.' — subordinate clauses of a stated condition, orphaned from their parent when the 'providing a credit service where the licensee is not or will not be:' heading is dropped by regex_extract. The heading-dropping heuristic therefore over-deletes (loses the parent activity) and under-deletes (keeps the dependent fragments), so the emitted set is not the publisher's authorised activities. Also, rows 550376/509306 mix 'as an intermediary' clauses with credit-provider/lessor clauses that belong to a different authorisation block, and 219612/465643 emit byte-truncated values ending in '...' (e.g. 'under which the licensee is the credit pr...'), so the emitted string is cut off mid-word. Transform errors are reported as zero but the output is semantically incomplete.

Role and target are defensible (lat/lon alongside the licensee's own address columns → ext.entity.address_point on the subject business, not an establishment), and geo_point dropping out-of-Australia coordinates is reasonable. But two issues: the coordinates are locality/suburb centroids (e.g. -33.8698439,151.2082848 repeated across unrelated Sydney licensees 550376, 509306, 225759 in one run; -37.83344,144.9570533 a locality centroid), so the claim asserts a business address point that the source does not support — the ontology says the point is of the business's OWN stated address, and a suburb centroid is not that. The caveat is documented, but no validity/confidence field is visible on the emitted observation in these held-out outputs, so consumers cannot distinguish centroid from rooftop. Precision should be either surfaced on the claim or the rule dropped for these values.

CRED_LIC_STATUS_HISTORY contains dated licence events ('Suspended at the request of Licensee/Registrant 19/09/2016 31/01/2017'), emitted on the licence role as multi-valued ext.licence.status_event with one entry per observation, matching the ontology. Dates are kept inside the free-text entry as published, which is acceptable given the noted absence of a reliable validity path; the event is not turned into a status enum and the suspension is not misread as company status or as a deregistration carrying valid_to. Note the licence-level status (APPR) is not overwritten by the historical suspension, which is correct because status events are historical.

missed.suggested_target: ext.licence.related_licence_number (only where value != CRED_LIC_NUM and value != '0')
missed.reason: Left unmapped with a defensible rationale (self-echo and '0' placeholder), and self-reference would indeed be wrong. But it is a genuine potentially-related-licence column: on rows where the value differs from CRED_LIC_NUM and is not the '0' placeholder it is exactly a related AFS licence number. A cleaner filter (equality test against the licence number, not a regex back-reference) would reclaim it; flagging as a missed opportunity rather than requiring the bad mapping back.

missed.suggested_target: ext.licence.valid_from / ext.licence.valid_to on the licence claim
missed.reason: These are already mapped (as observation.valid_from/valid_to in the approved set), so not truly missed; however the licence-start/end dates are the natural validity bounds for ext.licence.status and ext.licence.number. Since status and number observations here carry no validity at all, attaching the licence start/end to those licence claims would be more faithful than leaving them undated — worth confirming the approved validity lands on licence-scoped claims rather than record scope.

critic.summary: Rules 0, 1, 2 and 5 are sound: licence number, raw licence status, EDR scheme membership and dated status events all sit on the licence role with correct cardinality, and the licence status is correctly kept off entity.status. Two rules are doubtful. Rule 3 emits fragmented, orphaned and truncated authorisation text: the regex-based heading drop strips parent activities while keeping dependent 'where the service...' clauses and 'by providing debt management services.' fragments, and several values are byte-truncated with '...', so the canonical authorisation set does not represent the publisher's stated activities. Rule 4 maps locality-centroid geocodes (the same point repeated across unrelated licensees in one suburb) to the business's own address point without any surfaced precision marker on the claim, which overstates what the source supports. No entity_type guess, no person name emitted as a business name, no licence number used as a business identifier, and no legal/trading-name confusion appears in these held-out rows; CRED_LIC_BN values (FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE, KEYPLAYER FINANCE, DISCOVERY FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT) are handled by the already-approved trading-name rule and are plausible trading names here.

human_feedback: Rejected: (1) CRED_LIC_AUTHORISATIONS should also give the licensee's activity: the reviewed crosswalk anzsic_credit_authorisation maps the whole authorisation text (before splitting) to ANZSIC (credit provider vs credit assistance); add it as ext.entity.industry_code with scheme anzsic2006. (2) The authorisation split emitted ~10 fragments per licence, many of them lead-in headings ('This licence authorises the licensee to:', '... by:'); emit one observation per authorised activity and drop the headings, or keep the publisher's top-level '~' items only. (3) CRED_LIC_LAT / CRED_LIC_LNG are coordinates of the licensee's own address: map them to ext.entity.address_point (geo_point, latitude first) if the values support it. (4) CRED_LIC_STATUS is a code (APPR/SUSP); keep it, but its valid_from should not come from the licence start date unless the publisher dates the status. Keep everything else that passed.

licence.rationale: CRED_LIC_NUM is ASIC's credit licence number: 464/464 distinct on discovery, stated on every row, and stable across snapshots. The dataset grain is one licence per row.

relationships.rationale: CRED_LIC_NAME is the licensee that holds credit licence CRED_LIC_NUM; the licence is not the business, so it is a separate role held by the subject.

new_rules.rationale: ASIC register name of the licensee, presented as a registered-style name (mostly '... PTY LTD'/'... LIMITED'); some rows are individuals (e.g. 'TAN, JINTANG'), which are the licensee legal names of sole traders, not contact people.

ASIC 'business name' column, free of tilde separators, present on 34.5% of rows and clearly a trading/display name (e.g. 'DISCOVERY FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT' under LUNAWAVE PTY. LIMITED), not the registered name.

Mixed ABN/ACN column. Only the 11-digit shape (420/464 discovery rows, 90.5% ABN-checksum-valid) is an ABN by definition; regex_extract restricts the transform to that shape so 9-digit ACNs and 7-8 digit values resolve to null instead of raising ABN_LENGTH errors.

The 9-digit values (27/464 discovery rows, e.g. 601283201) in this combined ABN_ACN column are ACNs and pass the ACN checksum; passed through the checksum-validating acn transform. Taken from an explicit ACN value in the source, never derived from an ABN.
Suburb/locality column, 100% present, matches AU place names.
Two-letter AU state abbreviations, 8 distinct, all within the enum.
Licence start date, all values DD/MM/YYYY (day-first; values like 21/12/2010 and 28/02/2011 confirm day-first).
Publisher-assigned credit licence number, unique per row and stated on 100% of rows; identifies the licence across snapshots.

CRED_LIC_STATUS is the licence approval status (APPR on 464/464 discovery rows). It is licence status, not company status, so it must not go to entity.status. The licence start date dates the status claim. Kept as the raw code because the reviewed status tables (asic_company_status) are ASIC company codes, not licence codes, and no credit-licence label table exists.
External dispute-resolution scheme membership published for the licence; values are single codes or tilde lists (AFCA, COSL, FOS, AFCA~COSL...), so one scheme per observation.

values: This licence authorises the licensee to:

new_rules.rationale: The licence's authorised credit activities, published as tilde-separated prose lines with '; and/or' alternative lists. Splitting yields ~9.6 one-activity observations per licence with no transform errors. The publisher wording is retained; some fragments are lead-ins or conditions, so this is a lower-confidence narrative field.

AFS licence number of the same holder, stored as a separate licence role keyed by CRED_LIC_NUM rather than in the licence-number identity column. '0' (425/464) is the source's 'none' placeholder and becomes missing; 39/464 carry a real number.

Dated licence status-history entries (e.g. 'Licensee contravenes a licence condition 02/01/2013 ...') belong on the licence as status events, not on the business. Blank on 463/464 rows, so low volume, but the one populated value is a genuine dated licence event.

unmapped.reason: Constant 'Credit Licence' on 464/464 rows; identifies the register, not an entity, licence, or establishment attribute.

Latitude for the licensee address, but the values are locality-level geocodes, not premises coordinates: 37 unrelated licensees share -33.8698439 and 21 share -37.8142454 (315 distinct pairs across 464 rows). Mapping them as an establishment point would place a licence site at a suburb centroid. No establishment or premises role is declared because the source publishes a single business address, not a site.
Longitude paired with CRED_LIC_LAT; same locality-centroid evidence (repeated coordinate pairs across unrelated licensees). Not a premises location, so no geo_point claim is made.
